Package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery

Class BeanQuery

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery.BeanQuery
Direct Known Subclasses:
BeanQueryRequest
public class BeanQuery extends Object
A protocol-agnostic query request against a collection of beans: what to search, which columns to return, how to sort, and which page to return (design §5.1, §5.3).

Every field is a plain raw value — there are no HTTP-binding annotations, no Optional, no search map, no page string, and no parsed operators on this bean. A null field means absent. The grammar for search and opts lives inside those single strings and is decoded by a session when the query runs, not by this bean.

Fields
  • search (String) — the one search string. Top-level commas (outside parentheses) separate clauses; the first unescaped = separates a column from its raw $-expression (SearchExpressionParser); backslash escapes \, / \= / \\ are literals. Columns combine with and. See ClauseParser.
  • view (String) — a comma-separated list of column names, in output order.
  • sort (String) — a comma-separated list of column (ascending) or column:desc tokens (a trailing -/+ is also accepted).
  • position (Integer) — the 0-based first row of the page, or null for the start.
  • limit (Integer) — the page size, or null for all rows.
  • opts (String) — an open bag of key=value clauses (same grammar as search). The session reads counts and ignores unknown keys.

Construct with create(), which returns a BeanQuery.Builder that assembles these raw strings fluently:

Example:

BeanQuery q = BeanQuery.create() .eq("status", "active") .or(g -> g.contains("name", "bob").contains("email", "bob")) .sort("name") .limit(50) .build();

The HTTP-binding BeanQueryRequest (juneau-rest-common) extends this class and adds the @Query bindings.

Since:
10.0.0

    • copy

      public BeanQuery.Builder copy()
      Creates a BeanQuery.Builder pre-populated with this query's current state, so individual settings can be changed or added without disturbing the rest. getSearch() is re-parsed into the builder's item tree, so a new condition on an existing top-level column merges through $and(...) rather than being dropped or duplicated.
      Returns:
      A new builder seeded from this query.
